question.text: An indemnification clause in an AIF investment agreement:

answer.text: Requires the AIF to pay for all company expenses
Provides monetary compensation to the AIF if the company or promoter breaches representations or warranties
Is only applicable to listed company investments

explanation.text: The Logic: An indemnification clause in an investment/definitive agreement obligates the company or its promoters to compensate the AIF financially if representations, warranties, or covenants given at signing/closing turn out to be inaccurate or are subsequently breached. It is a contractual loss-shifting remedy and is typically subject to negotiated caps, baskets, time limits, and exclusions. The Trap: An indemnity does not require the AIF to pay company expenses (option A), does not eliminate investment risk (option C), and is not restricted to listed-company investments (option D). It is a standard feature of private investment agreements across listed and unlisted deals. Note: The specific claim that an AIF investment-agreement indemnification clause provides monetary compensation for company/promoter breach of representations or warranties is not explicitly stated in the cited workbook chapter (Series XIX-A_AIF (Category I and II) Distributors_Dec-version PDF.pdf, pp. 145-152, 190, 218, 269). The framing above is general industry/legal practice for definitive-agreement indemnities.
